title: Period of Insurance on a Travel Protection Plans Certificate
content:
Cancellation cover on a Travel Protection Plans certificate runs from the moment the certificate is issued, and every other benefit runs from the moment the insured journey begins until the moment it ends.

A journey begins when the traveller leaves their home address for the first booked departure and ends when they return to it, so cover is not tied to the booked flight times alone.

Where the return is delayed by an event the policy covers, cover extends automatically for the days of the delay at no further premium, up to the plan's maximum journey length.

A multi-trip plan covers each journey separately up to the plan's maximum length; a journey that runs longer is covered for the plan's maximum and not beyond.

Cover expires at the end of the last day of the journey and is never extended for convenience.

War and civil unrest are excluded on every plan, and an epidemic or a terrorist incident is covered only on a plan that says so.

## When each benefit is on risk

The cancellation benefit and the rest of the cover do not attach at the same moment. From issue until the journey begins, the cancellation benefit alone is on risk. From the moment the traveller leaves home for the first booked departure, every benefit of the plan is on risk. At the moment the traveller returns home, the journey ends and cover with it.

Because the journey is measured door to door, a traveller who leaves home some hours before the booked departure is already on risk for the whole of the plan, and a traveller still travelling home after the booked arrival is on risk until they reach it.

## The automatic extension read through

Suppose a journey whose return is delayed by four days by an event the policy covers, on a plan whose maximum journey length is 30 days, the journey as booked having run 28 days. Cover extends automatically for the days of the delay at no further premium, but only up to the plan's maximum: the extension carries cover to the thirtieth day and no further, because the plan's maximum journey length is the limit of the extension as it is the limit of the journey.

On a multi-trip plan the same maximum is applied journey by journey. A journey that runs longer than the plan's maximum is covered for that maximum and the remainder of it is not covered, and the next journey of the year begins its own count.

No extension is given for convenience: where the delay is not an event the policy covers, cover expires at the end of the last day of the journey as it stands.
